svg.title: Lab 06 — PAT and static port forwarding
svg.desc: Many inside hosts share one public IP outbound; one published port reaches an inside server inbound
svg.text: Lab 06 — PAT and static port forwarding
Many inside hosts share one public IP outbound; one published port reaches an inside server inbound
Same source port, different PCs? PAT assigns a new global port
PC0 and PC1 both chose :50001 — .11 becomes :50002 so replies stay unique
first packet builds the translation row
dst global port → inside local address
dropped, unless a static rule exists
Outside-Client can browse to Router0's public IP on 8080 but cannot reach 192.168.1.100 directly — private space stays hidden.
Compare the inside local and inside global columns for every flow: that mapping is the entire NAT idea.
